title: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Incentive-Compatible AI training Under Renewable-Energy Constraints
abstract: arXiv:2609.15389v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As artificial intelligence systems increasingly rely on distributed and collaborative training, the energy footprint of these processes becomes a shared responsibility. Modern AI training often unfolds across heterogeneous compute nodes-ranging from cloud clusters to edge devices-whose energy availability is spatially and temporally variable. At the same time, renewable energy grids experience growing levels of excess generation, creating opportunities to align computational workloads with low-carbon energy supply. In this work, we develop a game-theoretic model of carbon-aware AI training in which autonomous agents strategically choose whether to participate and how intensively to train under limited renewable energy availability. Each agent balances diminishing learning returns, rewards for remaining within green-energy budgets, and penalties for grid consumption. translated_title: 可再生能源约束下激励相容AI训练的博弈论框架
translated_abstract: 随着人工智能系统日益依赖分布式和协作式训练，这些过程的能源足迹成为一项共同责任。现代AI训练通常在异构计算节点上展开——从云端集群到边缘设备——这些节点的能源可用性在空间和时间上均存在变化。与此同时，可再生能源电网的过剩发电量不断增长，为将计算工作负载与低碳能源供应相匹配创造了机会。在这项工作中，我们建立了一个碳感知AI训练的博弈论模型，其中自主智能体在可再生能源可用性有限的条件下，策略性地选择是否参与训练以及训练的强度。每个智能体需权衡边际递减的学习收益、保持在绿色能源预算内的奖励，以及消耗电网能源的惩罚。虽然我们的框架广泛适用于分布式AI训练，我们……
tldr: 本文提出一个博弈论框架，使自主智能体在可再生能源有限的条件下策略性地决定是否参与AI训练及训练强度，通过绿色能源预算奖励与电网消耗惩罚机制实现激励相容的低碳分布式AI训练。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a game-theoretic framework in which autonomous agents strategically decide whether to participate in AI training and how intensively to train under limited renewable energy availability, achieving incentive-compatible low-carbon distributed training through rewards for staying within green-energy budgets and penalties for grid consumption.
